problem: Real-world instance-specific image goal navigation suffers from a domain gap between low-quality robot-observed object images (motion blur, low resolution) and high-quality user query images; prior work (SuperGlue matching, SimView) was tested mostly in simulation on large objects and does not address this gap.
motivation: Robots must find a specific small everyday object (cup, bottle, book) shown in a user's phone photo, but robot crops are blurry and tiny. Users can supply only a few photos per object, while robots can collect many images, so a few-shot cross-quality alignment is needed.
key_idea: Fine-tune a pre-trained SimSiam encoder with contrastive learning plus an instance classifier over both robot-robot pairs and few-shot high-quality/low-quality pairs (CrossIA), with instance pseudo-labels from a 3D semantic map.
insight: Deblurring alone barely changes results (SR 0.275 vs 0.281 for SuperGlue; 0.293 vs 0.290 for SimSiam), so the gap is a domain gap rather than just blur. SimView, which fine-tunes only on robot images, collapses (SR 0.066 and 0.034 with deblurring), and latent-space plots show it separates query images from observations; adding the cross-quality loss in CrossIA raises SR to 0.751. More high-quality shots help (SR 0.421 → 0.646 → 0.751 for 1, 3 and 5 shots).
method: Data collection module: the robot explores, RGB is deblurred with MSSNet, FastSAM segments instances, and a voxel 3D semantic map with consistent instance IDs is built from depth and poses.
Object image extraction: ray tracing on the 3D map produces per-frame instance masks, which become bounding boxes for cropping object images and give instance pseudo-labels.

CrossIA fine-tuning: SimSiam (negative-free) with an added linear instance classifier; loss = sum of L_robot (low-low pairs: negative cosine similarity plus cross-entropy) and L_cross (high-low pairs, same form).
Few-shot supervision: the user provides 1, 3 or 5 phone photos per instance, used as the high-quality domain in cross-domain pairs.
Optional adversarial variant: adds a domain-adversarial classifier (DANN) to CrossIA.

Navigation module: compute encoder features for the query and all observed object images, pick the highest cosine similarity instance, take its voxel centroid, and navigate to a free area within 1.0 m.

setting.backbone: SimSiam (ImageNet/ScanNet pre-trained, fine-tuned with CrossIA) + MSSNet deblurring (frozen) + FastSAM (frozen)
setting.training_data: Pre-training on ImageNet/ScanNet; fine-tuning on 2011 robot-collected object images (145 instances) plus 5 iPhone photos per target instance (1/3/5-shot ablation); 1000 epochs, SGD, batch 256, lr 0.07
setting.observation: RGB-D (640x480 Xtion Pro Live) with camera poses on an HSR robot; query is a single iPhone RGB image
setting.action_space: Navigation to a target position selected on the 3D semantic map (free area within 1.0 m of the object centroid); evaluation is on retrieval only
setting.privileged: none (the robot explores the environment in advance to build the 3D semantic map and image database)

numbers.eval_set_note: 640 trials (20 instances x 32 query images); identification/retrieval from robot-observed images, not full navigation
numbers.extra: 5 high-quality iPhone images per instance; pre-explored environment; MSSNet deblurring
adds domain-adversarial learning; 5 high-quality images per instance
numbers.evidence: Table 1: CrossIA with [DANN] ✓ SR 0.753, MRR 0.820, MR 1.21

numbers_note: SR is printed as fractions (0.751); converted to percent in metrics. MRR and MR kept as printed. No standard benchmark; a custom real-world evaluation.
results: CrossIA reaches SR 0.751 / MRR 0.812 / MR 1.24, about 2.7x the SuperGlue baseline SR (0.275) and 2.6x pre-trained SimSiam (0.293). Deblurring gives no significant gain, and SimView fine-tuned only on robot images performs far worse (SR 0.066).
limitations: Requires users to supply a few high-quality images per target object, which does not scale to many objects.
Evaluation measures instance retrieval among robot-collected images (20 instances in a single 74 m² environment), not full end-to-end navigation success.
Relies on pre-exploration to build the 3D semantic map and database; small scale (one room, one robot).
builds_on: GOAT (Chang et al. object image database)
